alignments.note: Participle carrying the subordination, so the supplied *when* is its rule 7/86 helper; the supplied object *it* rides with the verb that requires it in English. Discontinuous under rule 15.
Substantival article before a prepositional phrase; the ASV compresses οἱ παρ' αὐτοῦ into *his friends*, and the nominal word is the article's (rule 22).
The preposition is compressed into the possessive and realized nowhere separately, exactly as rule 36's τὰ περὶ ἡμῶν → *our state*.
*out* realizes the ἐξ- preverb and rides inside the verb's unit (rule 106).
κρατῆσαι → *to lay hold*, headed on the meaning-bearing complement rather than the support verb (rules 17, 91).
Object pronoun; the supplied *on* marks the verb's government and rides with the governed word (rules 36, 106). Reading *lay hold on* as one phrasal verb is the competing analysis.
Recitative ὅτι, marked in English by punctuation alone (rule 43).
ἐξέστη → *He is beside himself*; subject and copula ride with the one verb, headed on the word carrying the idiom's sense. A head on *himself* is the competing reading.

review_notes: οἱ παρ' αὐτοῦ → *his friends*: the article takes the nominal, the pronoun the possessive, and παρά is unrepresented under rule 36's compressed-possessive clause.
